name: Laminopathy with Lipodystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for LMNA-related Lipodystrophy

criteria.description: Progressive loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue predominantly affecting the limbs and trunk with relative fat accumulation in the face and neck
Presence of insulin resistance, diabetes mellitus, hypertriglyceridemia, or hepatic steatosis
Identification of pathogenic LMNA gene mutation associated with lipodystrophy
Family history of similar lipodystrophic phenotype or metabolic complications
Mild to moderate proximal muscle weakness or myopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive partial lipodystrophy plus metabolic complications and confirmed pathogenic LMNA mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires genetic confirmation due to phenotypic overlap with other lipodystrophies.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Partial loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue in limbs and trunk
searchTerms: partial loss of fat under skin on limbs and trunk
reduced subcutaneous fat in arms and body
loss of fat tissue in limbs and torso

pathognomonic.symptomName: Relative fat accumulation in face and neck (pseudo-hypertrophy)
searchTerms: fat buildup in face and neck
pseudo-fatty appearance of face and neck
relative fat accumulation in upper body

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe insulin resistance with acanthosis nigricans
pathognomonic.notes: Skin hyperpigmentation commonly seen in insulin resistance
searchTerms: severe insulin resistance with dark skin patches
high blood sugar with insulin resistance
muscle weakness or mild muscle disease
mood disorders like depression and anxiety
mental health issues with sadness or worry

laboratory: Elevated fasting insulin and glucose levels indicating insulin resistance
imaging: Echocardiography revealing cardiac conduction abnormalities or cardiomyopathy
genetic: Pathogenic heterozygous mutations in LMNA gene (e.g., R482W, R482Q)
other: Skin biopsy showing loss of subcutaneous adipose tissue
Electromyography may show mild myopathic changes

distinguishingFeatures: Congenital generalized lipodystrophy with near total absence of adipose tissue from birth
More severe metabolic complications presenting in infancy
Distinctive facial features and skin changes
Mutations in LMNA or ZMPSTE24 genes

redFlags: Rapid progression of insulin resistance despite standard therapy
Early onset cardiac conduction defects or arrhythmias
Severe partial loss of subcutaneous fat with metabolic syndrome features
references: Nishimura et al., Clinical and Molecular Features of LMNA-related Lipodystrophy, Journal of Clinical Endocrinology & Metabolism, 2020
